task.title: Place an image
task.shortdesc: Use the content property to make an element show an image, then give the image the size that you need.

info.p: Set content to a url() that names the file. The element shows the image, and what it contains is ignored:

step.cmd: Read the file name from your XML

info.p: When each element has its own file, keep the name in an attribute and read it with attr(). Add the type url so that CSSMedia reads the value as a file name:
This rule shows <figure src="images/pump.jpg"/> as the picture images/pump.jpg.
A file name can be written in these ways:

ul.li: A relative name in attr() is found from the location of the XML file, or from the xml:base of the element, if there is one.
A relative name in a url() of the stylesheet is found from the location of the stylesheet.
An absolute name can be a file: URL.
An http: or https: URL is downloaded when CSSMedia makes the PDF.
A data: URL holds the file itself, for example data:image/png;base64, followed by the data.

info.p: If CSSMedia cannot read a file, or cannot decode it, the box stays empty and the messages at the end of the run name the file.

step.cmd: Put an image in a line of text

info.p: An element is inline by default, so an image is a character of its line. Its bottom edge sits on the baseline of the text. Use vertical-align to move it. Set display: block to put the image on a line of its own.
A pseudo-element can hold an image too, which is useful for icons:

Without a width and a height, an image has its natural size, which is the size that the file has. One pixel of the image is one CSS pixel, or 0.75pt, so a photo of 1200 x 800 pixels is 900 x 600pt. Set width, height, or both. If you set only one, CSSMedia calculates the other to keep the proportions of the image.
A common rule keeps wide pictures in the page:

Files from cameras and scanners have many pixels for their size on paper. Use image-resolution to say how many pixels make a CSS pixel. The value is a resolution, such as 2dppx or 192dpi, and the initial value is 1dppx. The keyword from-image uses the resolution that the file states, when it states one:
The properties of Box sizes apply to images. An image without a natural size, such as a drawing with no width and height, is 300 x 150 pixels.
